children: Nairobi, Kenya, November 8th, 2026, Chainwire

Yiksi, a Kenya-headquartered fintech company developing solutions that connect local payment systems with digital finance, has secured regulatory authorisation in South Africa, marking a significant milestone in its ambition to expand access to digital financial services across African markets. Through its South African entity, Yiksi Fintech (Pty) Ltd, the company has been authorised by the Financial Sector Conduct Authority (FSCA) as a Category I Financial Services Provider in respect of crypto assets, under Financial Services Provider number 55213.

The authorisation establishes a regulatory foundation for Yiksi's expansion into the South African market, allowing the company to provide services within the scope and conditions of its authorisation. It also strengthens its position as it explores strategic banking, liquidity and payment partnerships to support its growing operations.

For Yiksi, the development represents more than an international expansion milestone. It reflects the growing role of African-founded fintech companies in building financial infrastructure that connects local economies to global digital markets.
Connecting African Payments to Global Digital Finance
Headquartered in Kenya, Yiksi is developing a suite of financial technology solutions designed to make digital finance more accessible and practical for individuals and businesses.

Its ecosystem includes Taran App, Yiksi Wallet and Yiksi Pay for Merchants, which are designed to help users convert between local currencies and stablecoins, facilitate cross-border transfers and enable businesses to accept digital payments.

These solutions address an important opportunity within Kenya's financial ecosystem, where mobile money and digital payments have become central to everyday transactions, while businesses and individuals increasingly engage in cross-border commerce and international markets.

For Kenyan entrepreneurs, merchants and businesses, the ability to connect familiar local payment channels with digital financial infrastructure presents opportunities to explore more flexible ways of managing payments, accessing digital assets and participating in the global economy.
As Yiksi expands across markets, its focus remains on developing solutions that bridge the gap between traditional payment systems and emerging digital financial technologies.
Building Trust Through Regulatory Accountability
The South African authorisation is also an important step in Yiksi’s commitment to building customer confidence through regulatory accountability.

As digital assets and stablecoin-based financial solutions continue to gain attention across the continent, regulatory clarity and responsible service delivery are increasingly important to the development of a trusted digital finance ecosystem.

“Securing FSCA authorisation as a Category I financial services provider for crypto assets marks a significant milestone for Yiksi. It reinforces our commitment to regulatory accountability and customer trust as we build accessible financial services connecting Africa to the global digital economy.”
Commenting on the milestone, Bile Ahmed Kabah, Founder and CEO of Yiksi, said:

“Securing FSCA authorisation as a Category I financial services provider for crypto assets marks a significant milestone for Yiksi. It reinforces our commitment to regulatory accountability and customer trust as we build accessible financial services connecting Africa to the global digital economy.” — Bile Ahmed Kabah, Founder and CEO, Yiksi

The company views its South African expansion as part of a broader regional ambition to develop financial solutions that respond to the needs of African consumers and businesses while connecting them to opportunities beyond the continent.

With its roots in Kenya and an expanding presence across African markets, Yiksi aims to contribute to a more connected financial ecosystem where individuals, merchants and businesses can participate in the global digital economy through accessible, familiar and trusted payment solutions.
